Nonsyndromic inherited sensorineural hearing loss.
PTPRQ-related nonsyndromic hearing loss; associated vestibular dysfunction belongs to the same ear axis.
Primary carcinoma of the supraglottic larynx; larynx belongs to the airway axis.
Primary squamous cell carcinoma arising in the thyroid gland.
Glycosylation defect with encephalopathy; visual impairment 2/2, optic atrophy 1/2, joint contractures 2/2; reflux 1/2 omitted by cap; direct lung injury unproven.
Intellectual disability with Coffin-Siris nail hypoplasia and digital abnormalities (2/2); ocular/endocrine defects vary; renal malrotation alone need not impair function.
Intrahepatic bile duct atresia causes obstructed bile flow; bile ducts belong to the hepatic axis.
Defined retinal capillary disease with macular thinning and progressive central visual loss; vascular involvement is localized to the retina.
Site-variable histologic umbrella, predominantly gastric; intestinal differentiation does not establish intestinal origin. Gallbladder and cervical sites are not universal.
Acute leukemia of myeloid and monocytic precursors; gingival infiltration is occasional (5-29%); dyspnea does not establish lung damage.
Fungal infection producing pulmonary lesions after inhalation of spores.
Inflammatory hypophysitis with histiocytic and lymphoplasmacytic infiltration of the anterior pituitary; no separate brain injury established.
Nonsyndromic X-linked intellectual developmental disorder.
Autoimmune neuromuscular junction disease; ocular and respiratory weakness reflect junction dysfunction rather than direct eye or lung injury.
Inherited corneal thinning and ectasia causing keratoconus and astigmatism.
Mature B-cell malignancy; lymphoma requires the immune mechanism axis. No extranodal organ site is specified.
Abnormally large gastrointestinal submucosal artery causes mucosal erosion and potentially severe bleeding; no primary blood-cell or coagulation disorder.
APCDD1-related hair follicle disorder with sparse hair in 19/19 patients.
Parasitic infection or infestation of the skin; systemic organ damage does not apply across most subtypes.
Primary osteoid-producing malignant bone tumor; intramedullary location does not make it a hematologic malignancy.
Congenital aortic vascular ring; tracheal and esophageal compression with impaired airway and swallowing function are defining effects.
GABBR2-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; seizures and intellectual disability in 2/2; hypotonia does not establish primary muscle disease.
